_comment: SYS procedures, verbatim from the 732A Instruction Manual (P/N 645051, May
1983) with the corrections of Change/Errata Issue 3 (7/85) written in and
cited beside the manual paragraph. Step text carries the manual's sentence
first; the connection description of the figure a step names, and any errata
note, follow it after an em dash, because the engine renders only step.text.
refs name SYS items (assembly-prefixed); the bare designators the manual
quotes in Table 4-3 are kept in refs and listed in sys.reference.json
foreignStepRefs so they are not offered as chips on SYS.
Sub-steps of §4-30 step 1 are numbered 1a..1f as the manual letters them.

procedures.title: Internal voltage measurements (Table 4-3)
procedures.prereq: §4-52: Use the tests shown in Table 4-3 to isolate problems to the major functional circuit groups of the 732A. It is assumed that the external symptoms given in Table 4-2 have been examined and that the primary circuit of the power transformer is operable. This procedure is conducted with the instrument energized, observe the previously stated WARNINGS and CAUTIONS. Table 4-3 footnotes: * Voltage measurements taken with Multimeter A, except for those marked with *** in corrective action column. ** Conditions: battery installed, BATTERY OPR switch ON. *** Calibration of 10V output affects calibration of this output. Each step names the board the points are on; the first point is taken as the meter's HI lead, the second as its LO lead - Table 4-3 does not say so; it is inferred from §4-44 steps 7 and 14 ("TP5 is positive with respect to TP1", "TP2 is positive with respect to TP1") and the nets on Figures 8-3 / 8-4. Table 4-3 prints no tolerances - the ones offered here are assumed and marked inferred.
warnings: TO AVOID ELECTRICAL SHOCK HAZARD, OBSERVE THE FOLLOWING PRECAUTIONS WHILE WORKING ON THE INSIDE OF THE 732A. REMOVE ANY JEWELRY BEFORE BEGINNING TESTING. HIGH VOLTAGE AC MAY BE PRESENT DURING THE FOLLOWING TESTS, DO NOT PERFORM ALONE. EXERCISE APPROPRIATE CAUTION TO AVOID ELECTRICAL SHOCK WHEN WORKING IN OR AROUND THE VICINITY OF THE AC POWER CONNECTOR, FUSEHOLDER, AND POWER TRANSFORMER. THE BATTERY ASSEMBLY IS CAPABLE OF GENERATING EXTREMELY HIGH PEAK CURRENTS. AVOID ACCIDENTAL SHORTING OF BATTERY TERMINALS. (§4-51 WARNING)

The following tests are conducted with power applied to the instrument. To avoid instrument damage, exercise appropriate caution to avoid inadvertently shorting adjacent test points or circuit board traces with test probes or other instrument(s). (§4-51 CAUTION)
To insure continued instrument performance, do not attempt to replace individual wires in the reference output wiring harness. Replace the entire harness. (§4-51 CAUTION)

steps.text: A3: TP3, TP4 - correct voltage reading ≤60V dc. Corrective action: AC line voltage, Rectifier, Power Transformer. — HI lead on A3 TP3 (+ output of bridge CR1, the raw rectified dc), LO lead on A3 TP4. The A3 Pre-Regulator PCB is in the rear-panel AC Module; the line connector, fuseholder and transformer are live.

A3: TP6, TP4 - correct voltage reading 32V dc. Corrective action: Pre-Regulator. — HI lead on A3 TP6 (+RAW, Q1 emitter after R1, the line to P3-2), LO lead on A3 TP4. §3-11: the Pre-regulator (A3Q1) is a simple emitter follower regulator that clamps the full wave rectified power from the bridge rectifier to approximately 32V dc. No tolerance printed; ±1.6 V (5 %) assumed.

A3: TP2, TP1 - correct voltage reading ≤31V dc. Corrective action: Battery Charger**. — ** Conditions: battery installed, BATTERY OPR switch ON. HI lead on A3 TP2 (charger output at the W1 jumper / R11 node), LO lead on A3 TP1 (-BATTERY). §4-44 steps 16-21 give the charger's behaviour: constant-current charge and the BTRY CHG indicator come on at approximately 26V (24.5 to 26.5V) and go off above +31V; then Q6 trickle-charges at approximately 27V at 23°C (§3-28).

A3: TP5, TP1 - correct voltage reading 33.0V dc. Corrective action: Battery Charger**. — ** Conditions: battery installed, BATTERY OPR switch ON. HI lead on A3 TP5 (Q6 base node - CR28 / R16 / R17 / RT1 junction, the trickle-charge reference; Q6's emitter goes through CR16 to +BATTERY), LO lead on A3 TP1. Set by R20 (§4-44 step 10: adjust R20 for a 33.0V dc reading; Figure 8-1 letters the pot R50). No tolerance printed; ±0.5 V assumed, as on the A3 dataset (the value is printed to a tenth of a volt, no limit is published).

measure.source: Table 4-3 row 4 (p42); §4-44 step 10 (p38). No tolerance published; ±0.5 V assumed, as on the A3 dataset

steps.text: A4: TP1, TP3 - correct voltage reading 32V dc. Corrective action: Pre-Regulator, Motherboard. — HI lead on A4 TP1 (the +RAW / 18.6V line at P2-12/13/14), LO lead on A4 TP3 (-RAW, P2-23/24). This is the A3 32 V after it has crossed A3 P3-2 / A2 J3-2 / J2-13 / A4 P2-13 and returned by P3-8 / J3-8 / J2-24 / P2-24: if step 2 passed and this fails, the fault is in that path on the motherboard or the connectors. No tolerance printed; ±1.6 V (5 %) assumed.

A4: TP1, TP2 - correct voltage reading ≈18.5V dc. Corrective action: Regulator. — HI lead on A4 TP1, LO lead on A4 TP2 (COMMON, the ground symbol at P2-2..5). §3-13: the Regulator (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) is a conventional series pass transistor error-amplifier design that regulates the 32V to 18.6V dc; on Figure 8-1 the pass transistor Q4 sits between the -RAW rail and COMMON. Printed with ≈ and no tolerance; ±0.5 V assumed, as on the A4 dataset, a band that contains the 18.6V the sheets print. When this rail falls below the critical value the voltage monitor shuts down the oven controller and latches IN CAL off (§3-15).

measure.source: Table 4-3 row 6 (p42): ≈18.5V dc; ±0.5 V assumed, as on the A4 dataset. Schematic 732A-1002 and Figure 8-1: 18.6V

steps.text: Front Panel: 10V, COM - correct voltage reading 10.00000V dc. Corrective action: Oven, Reference Supply. — HI lead on the 10V HI post, LO lead on the LO post beside it (Table 2-1 item 11, the 10V common). Table 4-3 gives no tolerance; ±6 ppm (±60 µV, Table 1-2 one-year transfer uncertainty) is offered as the widest published figure - the 30-day figure is 0.5 ppm. A 4½-digit Multimeter A cannot resolve this; the real verification is the null comparison of §4-37 or §4-39. The instrument must have been powered continuously with IN CAL lit; use low-thermal lugs clamped in the posts (§4-4 NOTE).

Front Panel: 1V, COM - correct voltage reading 1.000000V dc. Corrective action: Output Divider***. — *** Calibration of 10V output affects calibration of this output: check and set the 10V output first (Table 2-1 footnote). HI lead on the 1V HI post, LO lead on the second LO post (Table 2-1 item 12, common for the 1V and 1.018V outputs). Source impedance ≈1 kΩ (Table 1-2) - a low-impedance meter loads it. Tolerance ±12 ppm (Table 1-2, one year) assumed; adjustment A5 R59 (1V ADJ, ±5 µV) through the front-panel hole.

Front Panel: 1.018V, COM - correct voltage reading 1.018000V dc. Corrective action: Output Divider***. — *** Calibration of 10V output affects calibration of this output: check and set the 10V output first. HI lead on the 1.018V HI post, LO lead on the second LO post (Table 2-1 item 12). Source impedance ≈1 kΩ. Tolerance ±12 ppm (Table 1-2, one year) assumed; adjustment A5 R58 (1.018V ADJ, ±50 µV) through the front-panel hole.

Rear Panel: EXT. PWR. - correct voltage reading ≥24V dc. Corrective action: Battery. — HI lead on the RED (+) POWER INPUT jack, LO lead on the BLK (-) jack (from Rev C, J10 pins 1 and 2), with no external source connected: this reads the battery through the ballast lamp DS1 and CR1 / R1, whether or not BATTERY OPR is ON (§2-21: use a high impedance multimeter such as Multimeter A). Below 19 V the battery is being damaged (§2-22 CAUTION); a fully discharged battery needs 24 hours on line power (§2-24). Errata #12 step 27: with a known-good pack in trickle mode the charging voltage here is 25.8 to 27 volts.

procedures.title: Acceptance Test
procedures.source: §4-30, 4-31 (p32 / 4-8); step 1c as corrected by Errata Issue 3 (7/85) #7
procedures.prereq: §4-31: Use the following procedure to verify that the instrument is operational. The required test equipment is listed in Table 4-1. Equivalent instruments may be used, provided the minimum specification is met. (Table 4-1 marks for procedure A: Certified 732A - Fluke 732A; Four to Nine Cell Bank of Standard Cells - Guildline 9152P/4 or 9; Multimeter A - Fluke 8050A/8060A, 4½-digit display, 20 kΩ resistance range, 200 mV to 200V ac or dc; Adjustment Tool - Fluke P/N 686113. The Load Resistor 1 kΩ ½W Carbon Composition, Fluke P/N 108597, that step 5 uses is marked B, D in the table, not A.) §4-3: perform the acceptance test upon receipt of the instrument. §4-4 NOTE: use Fluke Low Thermal EMF Cable or copper wire with crimped and soldered low-thermal lugs clamped in the binding posts for all interconnections; avoid ordinary nickel-plated banana plugs. CAUTION: to avoid cracking the plastic binding post insulator, tighten only with finger pressure. Do not use tools.
warnings: To avoid cracking the plastic binding post insulator, tighten only with finger pressure. Do not use tools. (§4-4 CAUTION)

steps.text: Check the IN CAL indicator on the front panel. If illuminated, proceed to step 2. If not, complete steps a through f.

a. If the IN CAL indicator was not lit, set the rear panel BATTERY PWR switch to OFF and apply ac power to the instrument using the Variac, to the Supply Setting limit listed on the rear panel. — The manual's "BATTERY PWR switch" is the rear-panel BATTERY OPR switch (Table 2-2 item 5).
b. Adjust the Variac for 120V ac output. The ac line current should be less than 0.3A.

c. Set the BATTERY PWR switch to ON. The ac line current should be less than 0.35A. If the battery is very low, the BTRY CHG indicator will blink. — Text as replaced by Errata Issue 3 (7/85) #7. The May 1983 print read: "Set the BATTERY PWR switch to ON. The ac line current should be less than 0.35A if the battery is dead (BTRY CHG indicator blinking). If BTRY CHG indicator is on steadily, the ac line current should be less than 0.35A."
d. Allow the 732A to stabilize (under power) for 24 hours.

e. If a standards laboratory is available, perform the External Calibration Procedure described in Section 4. If a standards laboratory is not available, send the 732A to a Fluke Technical Service Center or an independent standards laboratory for calibration. — §4-32 Calibration: Procedure A (§4-37, certified 732A) or Procedure B (§4-39, standard cells).
f. Once the 732A has been calibrated, proceed to step 2.
Apply ac power of the correct voltage and frequency to the instrument. The AC PWR and BTRY CHG indicators should both be on.

Measure the value of the Oven Temperature Thermistor at the front panel binding posts with Multimeter A. The value should be within ±1 ohm of the value shipped with the instrument. — The two white OVEN TEMP THERMISTOR posts (E8/E9), RT2 inside the oven, 3 to 4 kΩ at operating temperature (§2-35); ohms, not volts. Errata #3: record the value to three significant digits in the instrument data log.

Check the output voltage at the 10V output using Multimeter A. It should be accurate within the performance limitations of the Multimeter. — 10V HI against the LO post beside it (Table 2-1 items 13 and 11).

Measure the change in output voltage under load. To make this measurement correctly, wire Multimeter A to the 10V and 10V LO binding posts (do not use plugs) and measure the voltage. Then plug the 1000 ohm load into the same binding posts and measure the voltage. The voltage change should be less than 50 uV or 5.0 ppm. — Load Resistor: 1 kΩ, ½W carbon composition, Fluke P/N 108597 (Table 4-1). Table 1-2: load regulation at 0.12 mA output current ≤6.0 ppm, output impedance ≤5 milliohms.
Repeat step 4 for the 1V and 1.018V outputs. — 1V HI and 1.018V HI against the second LO post (Table 2-1 items 10, 14 and 12). Both have ≈1 kΩ source impedance (Table 1-2).
If a standards laboratory is available, verify stability by comparison to standard cells or another pre-certified 732A. This step is optional.
The instrument is operational.

procedures.title: Null Verification
procedures.prereq: §4-36: Use the following procedure to verify the accuracy of null in the calibration procedures. The Null Verification procedure identifies the thermal voltages present and allows the null adjustment to be made independently of them. Use the Null Verification procedure in the two calibration procedures (Procedures A and B) when instructed to "verify the null". UUT = Unit Under Test; RU = Reference Unit (the Certified 732A in Procedure A, the Precision Divider output in Procedure B).

steps.text: Adjust the UUT for zero on the Null Detector.
Reverse the HI and LO (positive and negative) leads on the UUT and RU (Reference Unit).
Observe the Null Detector reading. If the reading does not equal zero, adjust the UUT for one-half of the Null Detector reading.

Reverse the HI and LO (positive and negative) leads on the UUT and Certified 732A. The Null Detector should have the same reading as it did at the end of step 3. If not, adjust the UUT for one-half the difference.
Repeat steps 2 through 4 until the Null reading does not change when the UUT and Certified 732A leads are reversed.
The residual reading on the Null Detector equals the sum of the thermal voltages in the circuit.

procedures.title: Procedure A: Calibrate to Certified 732A
procedures.source: §4-37, 4-38 and Figures 4-6, 4-7, 4-8 (p33-34 / 4-9, 4-10); figure grounding per Errata Issue 3 (7/85) #11
procedures.prereq: §4-38: Complete the following procedure to standardize the outputs of the 732A to a Certified 732A. Battery operation of the 732A and 845AB/AR is preferred. Set the Null Detector to ZERO when changing leads. Use the supplied adjustment tool for all adjustments (Fluke P/N 686113). Equipment marked B (Calibration, procedure A) in Table 4-1 (p26): Certified 732A - Fluke 732A (footnote **: calibrated at a calibration facility whose transfer uncertainties are consistent with the user's needs), Null Detector - 1 µV full-scale sensitivity, 10 MΩ input resistance, ZERO/OPR switch must open circuit input terminals in ZERO position - Fluke 845AB, AR, Multimeter B - 6½-digit display - Fluke 8500A, 8502A, Load Resistor - Fluke P/N 108597, Adjustment Tool - Fluke P/N 686113; Errata #6 adds the Voltage Divider - 7 decade, 0.1 ppm resolution - Fluke 720A (PROCEDURE C changed to B, C). The Adjustable Source - 10V dc output, 1 µV resolution - Fluke 5440A that steps 8-9 use is marked C only in the table. Errata #11 applies to every figure: delete the single connection between NULL DETECTOR GRD and GND and add a strap between NULL DETECTOR GRD and LO terminals. The 10V adjustment affects both the 1.018V and 1V outputs and is made first (Table 2-1 footnote).
warnings: Set the Null Detector to ZERO when changing leads. Use the supplied adjustment tool for all adjustments (Fluke P/N 686113). (§4-38; the potentiometers are reached through the front-panel 1.018V, 1V and 10V adjustment holes, Table 2-1 items 1-3.)

steps.text: Perform the self-calibration procedure on the Precision Divider immediately prior to this procedure.
Obtain a certified 732A.

Connect the UUT and the Certified 732A as shown in Figure 4-6. — Figure 4-6, 732A Procedure 'A' 10V Calibration (p33): CERTIFIED 732A 10V post wired (twisted pair) to the Null Detector HI post; UUT 10V post wired (twisted pair) to the Null Detector LO post; CERTIFIED 732A LO post wired along the bottom of the figure to the UUT LO post; CERTIFIED 732A GND post wired to the Null Detector GRD post, with the shield tail of the Certified-side pair on that ground wire; the UUT GRD post carries only the shield tail of the UUT-side pair; CERTIFIED 732A GRD and UUT GND have no wires. Errata #11: delete the single connection between NULL DETECTOR GRD and GND and add a strap between NULL DETECTOR GRD and LO. (The two 10 V outputs are thus in series opposition across the null detector.)
Set OPR switch on the Null Detector to the ZERO position, then switch power on. Adjust the Null Detector for zero on the 3 µV range.
Set the Null Detector to the 30µV range and the OPR switch to OPR.

Decrease the range setting on the Null Detector slowly while adjusting the 10V calibration potentiometer, through the front panel opening on the UUT, for a null indication on the Null Detector on the 3µV range. Let the system stabilize for about 1 minute before adjustment. Use the non-conducting adjustment tool supplied with instrument. — The 10V calibration potentiometer is A5 R20 (Figure 8-1 "10V ADJ"), range ±50 µV, resolution <0.05 ppm (Table 1-2). If the null cannot be reached, the coarse adjustment is by jumpers on the A7 Calibration PCB (§3-19).
Verify the null. — §4-35 Null Verification, steps 1-6.

Connect the equipment as shown in Figure 4-7. Set the Precision Divider ratio switches to 0.999999X. — Figure 4-7, Calibration of Point A to 10V Using 732A (p34): ADJUSTABLE SOURCE HI and SENSE+ both wired to the Precision Divider 1.0 input (the 1.1 terminal has no wire; the circled A beside 1.0 is 'Point A'), SENSE- and LO both wired to the Precision Divider LO input; the divider's output HI to the Null Detector HI (twisted pair); the divider's output LO wired along the bottom of the figure to the 732A RU LO post; 732A RU 10V post wired (twisted pair) to the Null Detector LO; source GRD/GND jumpered, GND to the Null Detector GRD and to the shields; RU GRD on the shield tail of its pair, RU GND unwired; ratio 0.999999X. Errata #11: strap NULL DETECTOR GRD to LO, not to GND. RU here is the UUT just calibrated (§4-33: the 10V output of the UUT is transferred to a stable adjustable voltage source).
Adjust the Adjustable Source for a null indication.
Verify the null. — §4-35 Null Verification.

Connect the equipment as shown in Figure 4-8. Set the Precision Divider ratio switches to 0.1018000. — Figure 4-8, Calibration of 1.018V (and 1V) to 732A Procedure 'A' (p34; caption misprinted 1.081V): same source-to-divider wiring as Figure 4-7 (HI/SENSE+ to 1.0, 1.1 unused, SENSE-/LO to LO), ratio 0.1018000 (0.1000000); divider output HI to the Null Detector HI; Null Detector LO wired (twisted pair) to the UUT 1.018V terminal; divider output LO wired along the bottom of the figure to the UUT middle-row LO terminal; UUT GRD on the shield tail of its pair; UUT 10V, top-row LO and GND have no wires. Errata #11: strap NULL DETECTOR GRD to LO, not to GND. NOTE on the figure: MOVE 1.018V ON UUT TO 1V FOR 1V CALIBRATION.
Set the Null Detector RANGE switch to the 3 volt range, then connect the Input lead to the UUT 1.018V terminal. Switch the Null Detector to OPR.

Adjust the 1.018V calibration potentiometer on the UUT while decreasing the RANGE setting on the Null Detector to obtain a null on the 3 µV range. Use the non-conducting adjustment tool. — The 1.018V calibration potentiometer is A5 R58 (Figure 8-1 "1.018V ADJ"), range ±50 µV (Table 1-2).
Verify the null. — §4-35 Null Verification.
Set the Presicion Divider ratio switches to 0.1000000.
Transfer the Null Detector input lead from the 1.018V terminal to the 1V terminal on the UUT.

Set the RANGE control on the Null Detector to the 3 volt position. Adjust the 1V calibration potentiometer on the UUT while decreasing the RANGE setting on the Null Detector to obtain a null indication on the 3 µV range. Use the non-conducting adjustment tool. — The 1V calibration potentiometer is A5 R59 (Figure 8-1 "1V ADJ"), range ±5 µV (Table 1-2).
Verify the null. — §4-35 Null Verification.

If the IN CAL indicator is illuminated, proceed to step 20. If not, connect a short wire to one of the front panel COMMON terminals. Momentarily touch the other end of this wire to the circuit board behind the RESET hole. The IN CAL indicator should illuminate. — COMMON terminals = the LO posts. The RESET pad is A1 LED PCB pad 15 (GRN), wired to A4 P2-19; touching it to COMMON relights the Q6/Q7 latch (§3-16).
Calibration is complete. Record all test results. Disconnect all test equipment. Cover the output adjustment access holes and the RESET hole with tamper-proof calibration seals.

procedures.title: Procedure B: Calibration to Standard Cells
procedures.source: §4-39, 4-40 and Figures 4-9, 4-10, 4-11 (p34-38 / 4-10 to 4-14); figure grounding per Errata Issue 3 (7/85) #11
procedures.prereq: §4-40: Use the following procedure to standardize the output of the 732A. Set the Null Detector to ZERO when changing leads or when not making measurements to avoid accidental damage to the Standard Cells. Observe the techniques presented in Section 2 for minimizing thermal emf errors. CAUTION: To prevent damage to the standard cells, the null detector used must open circuit its input leads when the ZERO/OPR Switch is set to the ZERO position. Equipment (Table 4-1, procedure C): Four to Nine Cell Bank of Standard Cells (Guildline 9152P/4 or 9), Voltage Divider 7 decade, 0.1 ppm - Fluke 720A, Null Detector - Fluke 845AB/AR, Adjustable Source 10V dc, 1 µV resolution, 0.3 ppm + 2 µV - Fluke 5440A, Adjustment Tool 686113. Errata #11 applies to Figures 4-9 to 4-11: delete the single connection between NULL DETECTOR GRD and GND and add a strap between NULL DETECTOR GRD and LO terminals.
warnings: To prevent damage to the standard cells, the null detector used must open circuit its input leads when the ZERO/OPR Switch is set to the ZERO position. (§4-40 CAUTION)

steps.text: Perform the self-calibration procedure on the Precision Divider immediately prior to this procedure.
Measure the standard cell enclosure temperature per the manufacturer's instructions and compute the voltage of up to 9 standard cells connected in series. Call this voltage S.
Set the Null Detector to the ZERO position.

Connect the equipment as shown in Figure 4-9A. — Figure 4-9, 732A 10V Calibration Using Standard Cells (p36), sub-figure A: ADJUSTABLE SOURCE HI and SENSE+ both wired to the Precision Divider 1.0 input (1.1 unused), SENSE- and LO both wired to the divider LO input, GRD and GND jumpered, GND to the Null Detector GRD and the shields; the divider's output HI to the Null Detector HI (twisted pair); STANDARD CELLS + terminal to the Null Detector LO and - terminal to the divider's output LO (twisted pair). The ratio printed on the divider is 0.999999X in sub-figure A and S10 (S/10) in B and C, as drawn. Errata #11: strap NULL DETECTOR GRD to LO instead of to GND.
Adjust the ZERO control on the Null Detector for a zero indication on the 3 µV range.
Set the RANGE switch to the 300uV range.
Set the Precision Divider ratio switches to S/10.
Adjust the Adjustable Source for precisely 10V output.

Set the Null Detector to OPR. If the Null Detector reading exceeds ± 300 µV, quickly return the Null Detector to the ZERO position and determine the reason for the imbalance. — NOTE: If a high degree of imbalance exists, check the output of the Precision Divider at its output terminals using Multimeter A. It should be approximately equal to the total voltage of the Standard Cell bank, or S.
Adjust the Adjustable Source for a null indication on the Null Detector. This is a preliminary null.
Set the Null Detector to the ZERO position on the 3 uV range. Adjust the ZERO control if necessary for a zero indication.

Disconnect the lead going from the positive terminal of the Standard Cells to the Null Detector at the Standard Cell end as shown in Figure 4-9B. Connect this lead to the negative terminal of the Standard Cells at the standard cell enclosure as shown in Figure 4-9C. — Figure 4-9B: a hand grasps the lead at the Standard Cells, lifting it from the + terminal. Figure 4-9C: the + terminal is left unconnected and the lead is on the - terminal, so the Null Detector sees only the lead and thermal offsets.
Set the Precision Divider ratio switches to 0.000000.

Set the Null Detector to the OPR postion and wait for a stable reading. Note any offset (residual reading). This reading represents the extraneous and thermal voltages which should be less than 0.5 µV. If the offset exceeds this value, the cause should be investigated and corrected before proceeding. Adjust the Null Detector ZERO control to obtain a null indication.
Return the Null Detector to the ZERO position. Do not disturb the setting of the ZERO control.
Set the Precision Divider ratio switches to the previously calculated value of S/10.
Reconnect the positive lead of the Standard Cells as shown in Figure 4-9A.
Readjust the Adjustable Source, if necessary, for a null indication on the 3 µV range of the Null Detector.
Do not change the setting on the Adjustable Source or the leads to the Precision Divider.

Connect the equipment as shown in Figure 4-10. — Figure 4-10, 732A Procedure 'B' 10V Calibration (p37): source and divider wired as in Figure 4-9 (HI/SENSE+ to 1.0, 1.1 unused, SENSE-/LO to LO; source GRD/GND jumpered, GND to the Null Detector GRD and the shields); divider ratio 0.999999X; divider output HI to the Null Detector HI (twisted pair); divider output LO wired along the bottom of the figure to the 732A UUT top-row LO post; UUT 10V post wired (twisted pair) to the Null Detector LO; UUT GRD on the shield tail of its pair, UUT GND unwired. Errata #11: strap NULL DETECTOR GRD to LO, not to GND.
Repeat steps 12 through 15 for the UUT. In Step 12, move the lead from the 10V HI terminal to the 10V LO terminal of the UUT.
Set the Precision Divider ratio switches to 0.999999X.
Set the Null Detector to the 300 µV range and set the OPR/ZERO switch to the OPR position.

Decrease the range setting on the Null Detector slowly while adjusting the 10V calibration potentiometer, through the front panel opening on the UUT, for a null indication on the Null Detector. Use the non-conducting adjustment tool supplied with the instrument. — The 10V calibration potentiometer is A5 R20 (Figure 8-1 "10V ADJ"), ±50 µV; coarse adjustment by A7 jumpers (§3-19).
Adjust the 10V calibration potentiometer to obtain a null indication with the Null Detector on the 3 µV range. Let the system stabilize for about 1 minute before adjustment.

Connect the equipment as shown in Figure 4-11. Reset the Null Detector to the 3V range. — Figure 4-11, Calibration of 1.018V (and 1V) to 732A Procedure 'B' (p37; caption misprinted 1.081V): same source-to-divider wiring (HI/SENSE+ to 1.0, 1.1 unused), divider ratio 0.1018000 (0.1000000 for the 1V calibration), divider output HI to the Null Detector HI; Null Detector LO wired to the UUT 1.018V terminal; divider output LO wired to the UUT middle-row LO terminal; the UUT 10V and top-row LO posts have no wires; UUT GRD on the shield tail of its pair. Errata #11: strap NULL DETECTOR GRD to LO, not to GND. NOTE on the figure: MOVE 1.018V ON UUT TO 1V FOR 1V CALIBRATION.
Set the Precision Divider to 0.1018000.

Decrease the range setting on the Null Detector slowly while adjusting the 1.018V calibration potentiometer, through the front panel opening on the UUT, for a null indiction on the Null Detector. Use the non-conducting adjustment tool supplied with the instrument. — The 1.018V calibration potentiometer is A5 R58 (Figure 8-1 "1.018V ADJ"), ±50 µV.

Adjust the 1.018V calibration potentiometer to obtain a null indication with the Null Detector on the 3 µV range. Let the system stabilize for about 1 minute before adjustment. Verify the null. — §4-35 Null Verification.
Move the wire connected to the UUT 1.018V output to the UUT 1V output. Reset the Null detector to the 3V range.
Set the Precision Divider to 0.1000000.

Decrease the range setting on the Null Detector slowly while adjusting the 1V calibration potentiometer, through the front panel opening on the UUT, for a null indication in the Null Detector. Use the non-conducting adjustment tool. — The 1V calibration potentiometer is A5 R59 (Figure 8-1 "1V ADJ"), ±5 µV.

Adjust the 1.V calibration potentiometer to obtain a null indication with the Null Detecor in the 3 uV range. Let the system stabilize for about 1 minute before adjustment. Verify the null. — §4-35 Null Verification.

If the IN CAL indicator is illuminated, go to step 35. If not, connect a short wire to one of the front panel COMMON terminals. Momentarily touch the other end of this wire to the circuit board behind the RESET hole. The IN CAL indicator should illuminate. — (Continues on p38 / 4-14.) COMMON terminals = the LO posts; the RESET pad is A1 LED PCB pad 15, wired to A4 P2-19 (§3-16).
Calibration is complete. Record all test results. Disconnect all test equipment. Cover the output adjustment access holes and the RESET hole with tamper-proof calibration seals.

procedures.title: AC Line Voltage Change (§2-16 Line Voltage Selection)
procedures.prereq: §2-17: The Line Voltage Selector switches are located inside the instrument. Their setting is marked on the rear panel (See Figure 2-2). If the marked setting does not agree with the locally available ac power, the settings of the internal Line Voltage Selector switches must be changed. Refer this and all servicing to qualified personnel. §4-29: The 732A may be operated from 100V, 120V, 220V, or 240V ac ± 10%. The assigned line voltage may be changed to match the available source using the following procedure. Refer to Figure 4-5. Switch settings (Figure 4-5, dot = selected): 120V - S1 100/120, S2 120/240; 100V - S1 100/120, S2 100/220; 240V - S1 220/240, S2 120/240; 220V - S1 220/240, S2 100/220. Fuses (§4-27): 100V or 120V - MDL 3/8 (3/8A slow blow); 230V or 240V - MDL 3/16 (3/16A slow blow). §4-13 NOTE: the AC Module may be removed without loss of standardization provided the BATTERY OPR switch is ON and the battery is charged.
warnings: THESE SERVICING INSTRUCTIONS ARE FOR USE BY QUALIFIED PERSONNEL ONLY. TO AVOID ELECTRICAL SHOCK, DO NOT PERFORM ANY SERVICING OTHER THAN THAT CONTAINED IN THE OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS UNLESS YOU ARE QUALIFIED TO DO SO. (Section 4 WARNING, p25)

steps.text: Ensure that the battery is charged or an appropriate external ac or dc source is connected to the POWER INPUT jacks on the rear panel. This will maintain the unit's stanardization when ac line power is removed. The BTRY CHG indicator on the front panel will extinquish when the battery is fully charged and the 732A is stll connected to the ac power source. — Battery voltage can be read at the POWER INPUT jacks (≥24 V, Table 4-3). External source: 24-40V dc or 24-30V ac, floating (Figure 8-2 CAUTION).
Set the BATTERY OPR switch to ON and remove ac line power from the instrument.

Remove the AC Module. — §4-14: remove the screws securing the module to the rear of the instrument (marked C in Figure 4-2) and pull the module out from the rear. The AC Module carries the A3 Pre-Regulator PCB (Table 2-2 item 1).

Locate the voltage selector switches (slide switches, top of PCB, near rear panel). Set the switches so that the dots on the switch actuators select the correct line voltage. As shown in Figure 4-5. — S1 legend 220/240 | 100/120; S2 legend 100/220 | 120/240 (Figure 4-5; Figure 8-3 draws them as two 2-pole switches). Settings: 120V - S1 100/120, S2 120/240; 100V - S1 100/120, S2 100/220; 240V - S1 220/240, S2 120/240; 220V - S1 220/240, S2 100/220.
Reinsert the AC Module, replace the screws.

On the rear panel, change the mark to the appropriate box, under the SUPPLY/SETTING heading, to indicate the present power configuration. — Rear-panel legend: SUPPLY SETTING 90-132V AC ☐ 50-60Hz / 200-264V AC ☐ 30VA (Figure 2-2).

Replace the line fuse with one of appropriate value. — §4-27: 100V or 120V ac operation MDL 3/8 (3/8A slow blow); 230V or 240V ac operation MDL 3/16 (3/16A slow blow). Rear panel: FOR FIRE PROTECTION REPLACE ONLY WITH A 250V FUSE OF THE INDICATED VALUE. Table 5-4 lists F1 FUSE, SLO-BLO, 3/8 AMP (109264) only; §2-19 prints 1/4A for 220-240V - see the caveat.
After verifying that the local ac line voltage matches the voltage selected on the 732A, apply ac line power to the instrument. — The AC PWR indicator should light (Table 2-1 item 4).
